S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.

subtypes.Unrestrained Buying Sprees: Spending excessive amounts of money or shopping recklessly to a degree that creates financial distress for self and family.
subtypes.Foolish Business Investments: Making rash business investments or ventures without sufficient review.
subtypes.Sexual Indiscretions: Engaging in indiscriminate or risky sexual behavior that is out of character.
subtypes.Impulsive Risky Behavior: Excessively dangerous or foolish behavior, such as reckless driving or drug use, without considering the consequences.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar II Disorder is characterized by a recurrent course of major depressive episodes and hypomanic episodes, with no history of full manic episodes. Hypomanic episodes involve a sustained period of elevated, expansive, or irritable mood and increased activity or energy that is observable by others but not severe enough to cause marked impairment or require hospitalization. Depressive episodes tend to be prominent and often drive help‑seeking, with significant impact on functioning and quality of life. Compared with Bipolar I Disorder, Bipolar II often presents with less dramatic mood elevation but more chronic or recurrent depression, and it can be misdiagnosed as unipolar depression if hypomanic periods are not carefully elicited.

patient.personality: Janice is a competitive, data‑driven retail leader with a strong creative streak, who thrives on visual projects and late‑night brainstorming but tends to run herself hard when chasing new goals.
patient.stressor: In the past year, Janice finalized a difficult divorce while simultaneously taking on expanded responsibilities at her store as she positioned herself for a regional district‑manager role. With her evenings now largely her own, she began filling the time with ambitious merchandising plans, late‑night pottery and painting sessions, and extensive strategic planning for her career, telling herself that staying busy helped her avoid dwelling on the divorce. During a recent seasonal reset, she rode a wave of intense drive and creativity, sleeping only a few hours a night yet still showing up early to reorganize displays and coach her team, convinced she was finally hitting her stride. After several weeks of this pace, colleagues commented on how "wired" she seemed, and when she found she could no longer wind down enough to sleep more than a couple of hours despite feeling physically worn, she agreed to consult a psychiatrist at the suggestion of her primary care provider, who was concerned about the abrupt and sustained change in her sleep and energy patterns.
patient.chief_complaint: Lately I only sleep a few hours a night and still feel wired, like I just can’t shut my mind off.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, like someone turned the color down on my life after the divorce and no amount of work wins or compliments from my team can shake it off for more than a few minutes at a time.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to get genuinely excited about sketching new window layouts or throwing a new batch of bowls on the wheel, but now even when I drag myself to do them, it feels flat and mechanical, like I’m just going through the motions to avoid sitting alone with my thoughts.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Over the past several weeks I’ve had to remind myself to eat because I just don’t feel hungry, and I’ll realize at nine at night that all I’ve had is coffee and maybe a granola bar at my desk.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: For the last month my nights have been a mess—either I’m lying there with my brain racing about floor sets and promotion ideas until two or three in the morning, or I crash for a couple hours and then pop awake at 4 a.m. unable to drift back off no matter how exhausted I feel.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even on days when I technically slept, my body feels like I’ve just pulled three Black Friday shifts in a row—my legs are heavy, my head is foggy, and just walking the store to check endcaps wears me out more than it should.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I keep beating myself up, thinking I failed at my marriage and I’m failing my team now too, and I replay every small mistake at work—like misordering a fixture or snapping at an associate—as proof that I’m just not good enough and don’t deserve this promotion I’ve been chasing.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: More than I’d like to admit, I catch myself thinking it wouldn’t be the worst thing if I just didn’t wake up one morning, and on the really bad nights I have this quiet, tired thought of, “What’s the point of all this?” even though I haven’t made any plans to hurt myself.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: There are stretches where I feel oddly amped up and touchy at the same time—like I’m on a constant shot of espresso—chattering a mile a minute about sales numbers and display ideas, then snapping at people over tiny things like a crooked sign or a missed email.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: I’ve been buzzing around nonstop, starting a dozen projects at once—reworking the clearance wall, rewriting training checklists, reorganizing my kitchen cabinets when I get home—because I feel this restless push that I have to keep doing something or I’ll crawl out of my skin.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: Lately I’ll sleep maybe three or four hours, wake up before my alarm with my mind already spinning on new merchandising schemes, and instead of feeling tired I feel oddly charged, like I don’t really need to go back to bed even though my body is worn out.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: In the last month I’ve thrown myself into work like a woman possessed—volunteering for every extra project, scheduling back-to-back one-on-ones with my associates, and then coming home and staying up half the night mapping out a five-year career plan and redesigning my pottery Instagram, as if I can’t stand to waste a single minute.

S041.name: Painful_Consequence_Behavior
S041.description: Excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences.
S041.manifestation: During that really wired spell, I found myself making some pretty reckless choices, like putting a big chunk of my savings on a rushed online order for trendy fixtures I was sure would 'revolutionize' my section without clearing it with my boss, and driving home way too fast and distracted after late shifts because I felt invincible and couldn’t be bothered to slow down.
